VBO:0200889.summary: Bold, inquisitive and eager to learn, the Miniature Fox Terrier is an animated little hunter with a quick spring and an abrupt change of direction. Australian Mini Foxies worked around farm homesteads controlling vermin. The Mini Foxie Club formed in 1986 to preserve that population and still maintains its own standard and registry.
VBO:0200889.shortDescription: A bold, inquisitive Australian homestead terrier, quick to spring into a chase and eager to learn.

sources.title: Mini Foxie Club of Australia — own breed standard
sources.evidence: Fearless bold confident eager to learn, inquisitive playful swift natural hunter able to spring/change direction. Adult24–30.5cm square balanced smooth small athletic terrier, gently wedge semi-flat head, small erect or soft-forward-fold ears, straight fine strong forelimbs/powerful bent hindlimbs/compact oval semi-hare feet. Long gradually tapering natural tail allowed, not overback/permanentcurl or belowhock relaxed; natural bobtails also allowed but photograph stump cause unknown. Predominantly white body, wellcolored black/tan head, SINGLE short dense fine glossy coat. Health/lifespan/suitability and breeder-exclusivity assertions unused.

VBO:0200879.summary: Alert and keen to learn, the Miniature American Eskimo Dog is an attentive companion whose warning bark often announces a visitor. It may be reserved at first with strangers while engaging readily with its people. The miniature is the middle of three maintained sizes, all sharing one breed standard.
VBO:0200879.shortDescription: An alert, quick-learning companion in the middle Eskimo size, often vocal about visitors and reserved at first.

VBO:0201358.summary: Friendly, alert and eager to please, the Toy American Eskimo Dog brings a quick-learning companion’s character to the breed’s smallest size. Its watchfulness includes barking at arrivals, and it can be conservative when meeting strangers. Toy Eskimos share one breed standard with the miniature and standard sizes.
VBO:0201358.shortDescription: An alert, eager-to-please toy companion, quick to learn and inclined to announce visitors with a warning bark.

VBO:0200359.summary: Cheerful and affectionate, Chorkies often form close bonds with their people. They can also be lively, assertive little companions, quick to bark when something disturbs them. These small Yorkshire Terrier–Chihuahua crosses vary considerably in both appearance and temperament, with no single fixed coat or ear carriage.
VBO:0200359.shortDescription: A cheerful Yorkshire Terrier–Chihuahua cross, often affectionate with its people and vocal about disturbances.
